findings.rule: Route bypasses the application layer / reaches into infrastructure
findings.explanation: The route constructs DigestsRepository itself and queries it directly, skipping DigestsService entirely (which already implements buildDigest). Presentation may only call the service; only the composition-root pattern (service built from the container) may wire infrastructure.
findings.fix: Instantiate DigestsService once in digestRoutes (from app.container) and have the handler call service.buildDigest(workspaceId, repoId, days); delete the repository import and construction from routes.ts.

findings.rule: Business logic in the route (routes are thin)
findings.explanation: Severity aggregation and top-files ranking are computed inline in the HTTP handler — orchestration/domain logic living in presentation, duplicating the logic that already exists in helpers.toDigestDto.
findings.fix: Remove the inline aggregation; let the service return the DTO produced by toDigestDto in helpers.ts, and have the route just return the service result.

findings.rule: Map at the boundary — raw Drizzle rows leaked to HTTP
findings.explanation: The handler returns raw ReviewRunRow/FindingRow arrays (including internal columns like workspaceId) in an ad-hoc shape instead of the DigestDto defined by digestSchema in vendor/shared/contracts/digest.ts; the contract and helpers mapping are bypassed.
findings.fix: Return the DigestDto from the service (built via toDigestDto) and attach digestSchema as the route's response schema so the wire shape is the Zod contract, never table rows.

findings.rule: External I/O not behind a container port (ports & adapters, composition root)
findings.explanation: The service performs cross-process I/O by calling the Resend mail API with a raw fetch and reads the secret straight from process.env.RESEND_API_KEY, hard-wiring a vendor into the application ring, bypassing SecretsProvider, and making the service unmockable.
findings.fix: Define a server-local Mailer port beside its adapter (adapters/mailer/index.ts), implement it there using the key obtained via the container's SecretsProvider, wire it in platform/container.ts with a ContainerOverrides slot, and have the service resolve it via this.container.

findings.rule: Application layer imports infrastructure (Db) instead of taking the Container
findings.explanation: DigestsService's constructor takes the Drizzle Db handle from db/client — the application layer may import domain, its own repository, and the Container, but not db/*. It also leaves the service unable to resolve any port (which sendDigest needs).
findings.fix: Follow the AgentsService pattern: constructor(private container: Container) { this.repository = new DigestsRepository(container.db) }, dropping the direct db/client import.
